title: 63 Years Ago This Week, Félicette Became the First Cat in Space - Nautilus
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAstronomy63 Years Ago This Week, Félicette Became the First Cat in SpaceShe’s still the only feline to have the honorDNBy David Nield10:00 AM CDT on October 21, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleOn October 18, 1963, French feline Félicette became the first “catstronaut” to head to space, landing safely by parachute after a trip of under 20 minutes.In that time, Félicette climbed to an altitude of more than 150 kilometers (93 miles) and experienced five minutes of weightlessness. It wasn’t enough to get into orbit, but it was comfortably higher than Blue Origin’s New Shepard went with Jeff Bezos on board, and about 40 percent of the way to the International Space Station.After months of training, Félicette was chosen from a group of 14 cats, apparently for her relaxed temperament. Ahead of the launch, the catstronauts in training were put into special harnesses for up to two hours a day to get used to the movement of spaceflight, while listening to sounds matching what researchers thought they would experience on the trip.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
